11	// ErrInsecureHTTP is returned when the base URL uses HTTP without an explicit opt-in.
12	var ErrInsecureHTTP = errors.New("refusing to use insecure http:// base URL for authentication (use --insecure-http-auth to override)")
13	
14	const (
15		// DefaultBaseURL is the production Entire API origin.
16		DefaultBaseURL = "https://entire.io"
17	
18		// BaseURLEnvVar overrides the Entire API origin for local development.
19		BaseURLEnvVar = "ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL"
20	
21		// AuthBaseURLEnvVar overrides only the auth/login origin (device flow,
22		// auth-tokens management, keyring key). Falls back to BaseURLEnvVar when
23		// unset, which is the right behavior for single-host deployments. Split
24		// hosts (e.g. auth on us.console.partial.to, data on partial.to) set
25		// both.
26		AuthBaseURLEnvVar = "ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL"
27

29		schemeHTTPS = "https"
30	)

32	// BaseURL returns the effective Entire API base URL.
33	// ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL takes precedence over the production default.
34	func BaseURL() string {
35		if raw := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(BaseURLEnvVar)); raw != "" {
36			return normalizeBaseURL(raw)
37		}
38	
39		return DefaultBaseURL
40	}
41	
42	// AuthBaseURL returns the origin used for the device-flow login, auth-token
43	// management endpoints, and the keyring key under which the bearer token is
44	// stored. ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL takes precedence; otherwise it falls back to
45	// BaseURL() so single-host deployments keep working unchanged.
46	//
47	// The result is canonicalised — lowercased scheme/host, default port stripped,
48	// path/query/fragment dropped, trailing slash collapsed — so the value that
49	// flows into store.SaveToken keys matches what tokenmanager.New emits after
50	// its own NormalizeOriginURL pass. Without this, a user setting
51	// ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL=https://AUTH.example.com:443/ would log in successfully
52	// (saved under the raw form) but every subsequent data-API command would
53	// resolve "not logged in" because the manager probes under the normalised
54	// "https://auth.example.com".
55	func AuthBaseURL() string {
56		raw := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(AuthBaseURLEnvVar))
57		if raw == "" {
58			raw = BaseURL()
59		}
60		return NormalizeOriginURL(raw)
61	}

63	// ResolveURL joins an API-relative path against the effective base URL.
64	func ResolveURL(path string) (string, error) {
65		return ResolveURLFromBase(BaseURL(), path)
66	}
67	
68	// ResolveURLFromBase joins an API-relative path against an explicit base URL.
69	// Only http and https schemes are accepted.
70	func ResolveURLFromBase(baseURL, path string) (string, error) {
71		base, err := url.Parse(baseURL)
72		if err != nil {
73			return "", fmt.Errorf("parse base URL: %w", err)
74		}
75	
76		if base.Scheme != schemeHTTP && base.Scheme != schemeHTTPS {
77			return "", fmt.Errorf("unsupported base URL scheme %q (must be http or https)", base.Scheme)
78		}
79	
80		rel, err := url.Parse(path)
81		if err != nil {
82			return "", fmt.Errorf("parse path: %w", err)
83		}
84	
85		return base.ResolveReference(rel).String(), nil
86	}

88	// RequireSecureURL returns ErrInsecureHTTP if the base URL uses the http scheme.
89	// Call this before making authenticated requests unless --insecure-http-auth is set.
90	func RequireSecureURL(baseURL string) error {
91		u, err := url.Parse(baseURL)
92		if err != nil {
93			return fmt.Errorf("parse base URL: %w", err)
94		}
95	
96		if u.Scheme == schemeHTTP {
97			return ErrInsecureHTTP
98		}
99	
100		return nil
101	}
102	
103	func normalizeBaseURL(raw string) string {
104		return strings.TrimRight(strings.TrimSpace(raw), "/")
105	}

107	// NormalizeOriginURL canonicalises an origin URL the same way auth-go's
108	// tokenmanager does internally: lowercase scheme/host, default port stripped
109	// (80 for http, 443 for https), path/query/fragment dropped, trailing slash
110	// collapsed. On parse failure, raw is returned unchanged so non-URL audience
111	// values still compare byte-for-byte.
112	//
113	// Mirrors auth-go's internal/oauthhttp.NormalizeOriginURL so the value the
114	// CLI hands to the manager as Issuer survives the manager's own normalisation
115	// pass byte-for-byte — see AuthBaseURL.
116	func NormalizeOriginURL(raw string) string {
117		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(raw)
118		u, err := url.Parse(trimmed)
119		if err != nil || u.Scheme == "" || u.Host == "" {
120			return trimmed
121		}
122		scheme := strings.ToLower(u.Scheme)
123		hostname := strings.ToLower(u.Hostname())
124		port := u.Port()
125		dropPort := port == "" ||
126			(scheme == schemeHTTP && port == "80") ||
127			(scheme == schemeHTTPS && port == "443")
128	
129		out := url.URL{Scheme: scheme}
130		switch {
131		case dropPort && strings.Contains(hostname, ":"):
132			out.Host = "[" + hostname + "]"
133		case dropPort:
134			out.Host = hostname
135		case strings.Contains(hostname, ":"):
136			out.Host = "[" + hostname + "]:" + port
137		default:
138			out.Host = hostname + ":" + port
139		}
140		return out.String()
141	}
142

144	// Callers reading raw URLs (e.g. ENTIRE_SEARCH_URL) and feeding them into
145	// tokenmanager.TokenRequest.Resource use this to strip path/query/fragment
146	// before the lib's stricter origin-only validator runs.
147	func OriginOnly(raw string) string {
148		return NormalizeOriginURL(raw)
149	}

You need three env vars before running `entire login`:

| Env var | Value | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `ENTIRE_AUTH_PROVIDER_VERSION` | `v2` | Selects the new auth surface (OIDC-standard `/device_authorization` + RFC 8693 token exchange). Without this you'll get v1's `/oauth/device/code` paths — see `cmd/entire/cli/auth/provider.go:42-65`. |
| `ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL` | `https://us.auth.partial.to` | The auth host that mints tokens (device flow + keyring key). |
| `ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL` | `https://partial.to` | The data API host that consumes tokens. |

The split-host setup is the whole reason `v2` exists — `v1` assumes auth and data share an origin and skips STS. `AuthBaseURL()` falls back to `BaseURL()` if you only set one, so for partial.to you need both (`cmd/entire/cli/api/base_url.go:55-61`).

```bash
export ENTIRE_AUTH_PROVIDER_VERSION=v2
export ENTIRE_AUTH_BASE_URL=https://us.auth.partial.to
export ENTIRE_API_BASE_URL=https://partial.to
entire login
```

Tokens are keyed in the keyring under the canonicalised `AuthBaseURL()`, so keep these env vars set for subsequent commands or they'll resolve "not logged in".

642	// partial clone.

645	// to a bare remote, then clones to a fresh repo that does NOT have the
646	// feature branch locally. With filtered_fetches enabled, `entire resume`
647	// must still fetch the branch fully so the checked-out file has real content.
648	func TestResume_FetchesPrimaryBranchFullyWithFilteredFetches(t *testing.T) {
649		t.Parallel()
650		env := NewFeatureBranchEnv(t)
651	
652		bareDir := env.SetupBareRemote()

654		// Create a session with a source file and commit it on the feature branch.
655		_ = createCheckpointedCommit(t, env, "Build auth module", "auth.go", "package auth", "Build auth module")

658		env.GitPush("origin", "HEAD")

660	
661		// Clone the repo, then switch away from the feature branch and delete it
662		// locally so it only exists on the remote. This forces resume to fetch it.
663		cloneEnv := env.CloneFrom(bareDir)
664	
665		ctx := t.Context()

Here's the review of PR #1258 ("Route auth status/list/revoke/logout through TokenForResource"):

## CI

The only failure is `TestResume_FetchesPrimaryBranchFullyWithFilteredFetches` in `test-integration (b)`. **It looks like a flake unrelated to this PR.** The test assertions all passed — resume succeeded, file content matched, transcript blob found. The actual failure is at framework cleanup:

```
testing.go:1464: TempDir RemoveAll cleanup: unlinkat /tmp/.../006/.git: directory not empty
```

That's `t.TempDir()` failing to remove the bare-remote `.git` dir (similar in shape to the `TestFetchAndRebase_*` flake we already have open with Paulo — handle/process holding onto git objects). The PR doesn't touch `resume`, `fetch`, or anything bare-remote related. Worth a re-run before merging; if it repeats, the test itself needs a bare-repo close/cleanup fix.

## The PR itself

Small (6 files), well-scoped, and the structural change is genuinely nice: dropping `token` / `callerToken` from `authTokenLister` / `authTokenRevoker` / `revokeCurrentFunc` makes the audience-mismatch bug **structurally impossible** at call sites. `resolveDataAPIToken` centralises the RFC 8693 exchange. Good shape.

Other pieces:
- `requireSecureBaseURL` now also calls `auth.EnableInsecureHTTP()` — matches what `NewAuthenticatedAPIClient` already does. Correct consistency fix.
- `api_client.go` wrap preserves the `ErrNotLoggedIn` sentinel across the boundary.
- `activity_cmd.go` stops swallowing real errors behind a misleading login hint.

## Issues worth fixing before merge

**1. `api_client.go:53` — dropped error context (Copilot caught this, agreed):**

```go
return nil, fmt.Errorf("not logged in (run 'entire login' first): %w", auth.ErrNotLoggedIn)
```

You're wrapping the sentinel instead of the actual `err`. If `TokenForResource` ever returns something like `fmt.Errorf("keyring permission denied: %w", auth.ErrNotLoggedIn)`, the prefix is lost. Simpler:

```go
return nil, fmt.Errorf("not logged in (run 'entire login' first): %w", err)
```

`errors.Is(err, auth.ErrNotLoggedIn)` still works because the chain is preserved.

**2. `auth.go:166` — split-host status UX (Cursor caught this, real concern):**

In `runAuthStatus`, the "Token in keychain for X is no longer valid" branch only fires for `*api.HTTPError` 401s. In v2 split-host, a revoked core token now fails inside `resolveDataAPIToken`'s STS exchange before any HTTP call to the data API — so the status command will show a raw STS error instead of the friendly "no longer valid" message. Worth adding STS-rejection detection to that branch, or the message it was supposed to produce becomes unreachable in the exact scenario this PR was written for.

**3. `activity_cmd.go:72` — context cancel surfacing (Cursor):**

`context.Canceled` from Ctrl+C used to be swallowed under the login hint; now it surfaces as a visible error. Probably fine (silencing was wrong), but if you want the old quiet-on-cancel behavior, gate with `errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)`.

**4. Test coverage gap (Copilot):**

The new `resolveDataAPIToken` path isn't exercised — tests inject fakes for `list`/`revoke`. Worth one focused test using `auth.SetManagerForTest` to verify the audience-matching actually happens. Not blocking.

## Verdict

LGTM structurally. Re-run CI to confirm the flake. Fix #1 (trivial, just swap the `%w` argument) and address #2 (the split-host status branch) — those are both in the same spirit as the PR. #3 and #4 are nice-to-haves.

143		}
